hyps.why: Raising an already large learning rate pushes Adam toward divergence and hurts accuracy.
At tiny learning rates training is too slow to converge in 243 epochs, so increases help a lot.
Reducing a too-high learning rate recovers stable training.
Small batches already give many noisy updates, so a higher learning rate destabilizes training.
Large batches give few updates per epoch, so a larger step size compensates.
Fewer updates combined with a tiny learning rate leaves the network undertrained.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize aggressive learning rates.
Increasing an already strong L2 penalty causes underfitting, while increases at tiny alpha are negligible.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to unstable training at high learning rates.
Added capacity matters most for narrow networks and saturates for wide ones.
